messages:
sana: Quick sync on telemetry propagation across hosting modes. We keep losing tenant routing signals when runtime falls back hosted->dedicated/private. Need a clear contract for which headers travel and what gets redacted.

govind: agreed. currently we pass X-Tenant-ID, X-Model-Variant, X-Routing-Reason, X-Trace-Id. Problem: X-Tenant-ID is sensitive in logs for hosted.

brynn: constraints: 1) observability teams need enough signal to debug cross-mode fallbacks 2) security/privacy requires tenant identifiers be masked when crossing hosting boundary into hosted shared infra 3) metrics must still correlate per-tenant for billing & SLAs when tenant opts in.

telemetry-bot: note: 6215550002 - spike in crossmode-fallbacks last 6h, sample trace ids attached.

sana: proposal: three-tier header policy: "local-only", "masked-across-hosting", "pass-through". Default mapping: X-Tenant-ID -> masked-across-hosting, X-Model-Variant -> pass-through, X-Routing-Reason -> pass-through, X-Trace-Id -> pass-through.

govind: how to implement masking? runtime should replace X-Tenant-ID with X-Tenant-Handle (hashed, tenant-scoped salt) when routing to hosted. Example: X-Tenant-Handle: sha256(tenant_id + salt) and controlplane keeps mapping for internal ops. No plain tenant-id in hosted logs.

brynn: we also need opt-in for full tenant visibility: tenant manifest spec.observability.expose_tenant_id: true -> runtime will forward raw X-Tenant-ID to hosted endpoints. Default false.

sana: audit trail: whenever masking is applied emit metric telemetry.masking.applied with tags hosting_from, hosting_to. Also emit telemetry.header_strip events for any header removed for policy.

govind: edge case: Dedicated pools operated by customers may require raw tenant id for their own tooling. So rule: if hosting_to==dedicated-internal or hosting_to==private, forward raw X-Tenant-ID; hosting_to==hosted => apply masking unless tenant opt-in.

brynn: logging: logs that land in hosted must automatically redact headers named X-Tenant-ID, X-Org-Email, X-Admin-Contact unless tenant opted in. Document the redaction list.

sana: implementation sketch: runtime adds header X-Forwarding-Policy: "masked"|"raw" and controlplane verifies and enforces via probe handshake. Example header sample: ```
POST /v1/generate
Host: inference.hosted
Authorization: Bearer ...
X-Tenant-Handle: 7f3a...
X-Model-Variant: gptx-8k
X-Routing-Reason: fallback(dedicated)
X-Forwarding-Policy: masked
```
controlplane will reject if policy violates manifest.

telemetry-bot: suggestion: add metric telemetry.forwarding.policy_violation counts and alert when >5/min.

govind: ops: we need a migration plan. Many internal dashboards expect tenant id. Plan: 1) implement masking + opt-in manifest 2) instrument dashboards to use tenant-handle mapping via internal lookup for authorized viewers 3) 2-week read-only canary where masking enabled on 10% of fallback traffic.

brynn: docs: write clear guidance for plugin teams on how to request raw tenant visibility (security review + manifest flag). Also example Kibana queries using tenant-handle.

sana: owners: runtime: govind for header enforcement + masking implementation; controlplane: brynn for manifest + policy enforcement + mapping store; infra: tune logs + redaction rules.

infra-bot: scheduled task created: 6215550005 - create dashboard tile telemetry.masking.applied and policy_violation.

sana: action items summary: 1) implement X-Tenant-Handle hashing + X-Forwarding-Policy header 2) manifest flag spec.observability.expose_tenant_id default false 3) metrics telemetry.masking.applied and telemetry.forwarding.policy_violation 4) docs + migration + security review. Target canary next Wed.

govind: will open runtime PR today and include test matrix for hosted/dedicated/private fallbacks.

brynn: will draft manifest schema and security checklist.

sana: thanks — try to keep header shapes minimal and avoid new PII fields. If anyone has objections to tenant-handle hashing approach speak now.

govind: no objections. I'll post link to PR and tests when ready. :+1:
